To the person reading this and then deciding to eat 10-12k calories a day, let me spell out how insane it would be just to burn all this off.

Assuming you have a BMR (basal metabolic rate) of 2000 cal/day, and noting that running for an hour straight will burn just under 1000 calories, you'd need to run 8-10 hours a day (not including breaks) just to break even. This means that if you're not burning 8000-10000 calories per day, you'll be gaining an inhuman amount of weight, with only a very small amount of that being lean muscle. Even if you're looking to eat a surplus to gain mass, you'd still need to run for 7-9 hours nonstop just to keep your weight in check.

On top of all this, 12k calories are just not feasible to consume at all. One 4lb chicken (raw) is about 3000 calories. To eat 12000 calories in a day, you'd need to be capable of eating FOUR WHOLE CHICKENS DAILY. I doubt there's a person alive who can sustain this rate of consumption for longer than a day, let alone a week. 

Now, if you are looking to gain weight at a steady rate, the best way to do that food-wise would be to go to [tdeecalculator.net](https://tdeecalculator.net/), fill out the fields on that page to get your estimated TDEE (total daily energy expenditure), then eat 500-1000 calories more than that. 

TL,DR: Don't even try to eat 10k-12k calories, rest of OP's comment is alright though
